title: Test for Differences in Diversification Rates over Time
text: R package deepSTRAPP employs time-calibrated phylogenies trait data test differences diversification rates traits evolutionary time. works continuous, categorical, biogeographic trait data extends STRAPP test [BAMMtools::traitDependentBAMM()] time step along phylogenies. deepSTRAPP provides powerful analytic framework investigate Rate Diversification Hypothesis (RDH) context Historical Biogeography. RDH posits current heterogeneity diversity patterns Latitudinal Diversity Gradient mostly due differences diversification rates across bioregions. hypothesis typically assessed comparing diversification rates across tips different bioregions example STRAPP test (Rabosky & Huang, 2016). However, tests compare current rates diversification mat informative long-term past dynamics shaping present-day biodiversity. deepSTRAPP overcomes methodological gap: enables test RDH comparing diversification rates time step along evolutionary time. typical outcome, allows researchers identify time-frame significance diversification rates different across trait values, providing quantitative testing framework disentangle effects past current dynamics explaining current patterns biodiversity. Beyond biogeographic context, deepSTRAPP can used test evolutionary relationship phenotypic evolution diversification dynamics type traits. provides alternative approach state-dependent speciation extinction (SSE) models intend model altogether trait evolution diversification dynamics, often time-consuming hard parametrize, especially large time-calibrated phylogenies. Conversely, deepSTRAPP offers flexible solution can applied phylogenies encompassing thousands lineages (Doré al., 2025). deepSTRAPP especially suited large phylogenies power statistical tests limited number diversification regime shifts detected phylogeny used perform permutation tests. macroevolutionary regime acts independent event used test differences, therefore sample size tests conditioned number macroevolutionary regimes identified. unlikely detect significant differences regime shifts. full deepSTRAPP workflow runs follows: Step 1: Map trait evolution Step 2: Infer diversification dynamics (typically BAMM) Step 3: Run deepSTRAPP Step 3.1: Extract traits values, diversification rates, regimes given time past Step 3.2: Run STRAPP test Step 3.3: Repeat steps 3.1 & 3.2 many timesteps along evolution time Step 4: Summarize tests results Figure 1: Simplified deepSTRAPP workflow showing main functions (italic) involved step 1 5. Input data grey. Data processing blue (main) beige (internal). Intermediate objects green. Final outputs pink. References: STRAPP test: Rabosky, D. L., & Huang, H. (2016). robust semi-parametric test detecting trait-dependent diversification. Systematic biology, 65(2), 181-193. https://doi.org/10.1093/sysbio/syv066. deepSTRAPP application: Doré, M., Borowiec, M. L., Branstetter, M. G., Camacho, G. P., Fisher, B. L., Longino, J. text: phytools functions, like phytools::countSimmap(), count anagenetic events (range transitions occurring along branches) written assuming purely anagenetic models. remains possible extract cladogenetic events (range transitions occurring speciation) comparing last-state---node descendant-pairs---node. However, recommended use built-functions BioGeoBEARS summarize biogeographic history based tables cladogenetic anagenetic events obtained BioGeoBEARS::runBSM(). simmap objects primarily considered tool visualization. Associated functions R package BioGeoBEARS: BioGeoBEARS::simulate_source_areas_ana_clado(): select randomly unique area source transition multi-area state single area. BioGeoBEARS::get_dmat_times_from_res(): generate matrices range expansion source area destination area. BioGeoBEARS::count_ana_clado_events(): count number type events BSM tables. BioGeoBEARS::hist_event_counts(): plot histograms event counts across BSM tables. Please note carefully area--area dispersal events identical state transitions. example, state can geographic range multipleareas, logic DEC-type models, range-expansion event like  ABC->ABCD actually means dispersal happened specific area (, B, C) new area. BSMs track area--area sourcing cladogenetic anagenetic event tables, least BioGeoBEARS::simulate_source_areas_ana_clado() run output BioGeoBEARS::runBSM().

Absolute time since root edge/branch start (rootward). $end Vector numerical.  Absolute time since root edge/branch end (tipward). $downseq Vector integers. Order node visits using pre-order tree traversal. $lastvisit ID last node visited starting node corresponding position $downseq. BAMM elements summarizing diversification data: $numberEvents Vector integer. Number events/macroevolutionary regimes (k+1) recorded posterior configuration. k = number shifts. $eventData List data.frames. One per posterior sample. Records shift events macroevolutionary regimes parameters. 1st line = Background root regime. $eventVectors List integer vectors. One per posterior sample. Record regime ID per branches. $tipStates List integer vectors. One per posterior sample. Record regime ID per tips. $tipLambda List numerical vectors. One per posterior sample. Record speciation rates per tips. $tipMu List numerical vectors. One per posterior sample. Record extinction rates per tips. $eventBranchSegs List matrix numerical. One per posterior sample. Record regime ID per segments branches. $meanTipLambda Vector numerical. Mean tip speciation rates across posterior configurations tips. $meanTipMu Vector numerical. Mean tip extinction rates across posterior configurations tips. $type Character string. Set type data modeled BAMM. , type = "diversification". Additional elements providing key information downstream analyses: $expectedNumberOfShifts Integer. expected number regime shifts used set prior BAMM. $MSP_tree Object class phylo. List 18 elements class `"bammdata" recording mean rates regime shift locations found across Maximum Posteriori probability (MAP) configurations. BAMM elements summarizing diversification data holds single entry describing mean diversification history. $MSC_indices Vector integers. indices Maximum Shift Credibility (MSC) configurations among posterior samples. $MSC_BAMM_object List 18 elements class `"bammdata" recording mean rates regime shift locations found across Maximum Shift Credibility (MSC) configurations. Record regime ID per segments branches. $meanTipLambda Vector numerical. Mean tip speciation rates across posterior configurations tips. $meanTipMu Vector numerical. Mean tip extinction rates across posterior configurations tips. $type Character string. Set type data modeled BAMM. , type = "diversification". title: Computes STRAPP to test for a relationship between diversification rates and trait data — compute_STRAPP_test_for_focal_time
text: Carries appropriate statistical method test relationship diversification rates trait data given point past (.e. focal_time). Tests based block-permutations: rates data randomized across tips following blocks defined diversification regimes identified tip (typically BAMM). tests called STructured RAte Permutations Phylogenies (STRAPP) described Rabosky, D. L., & Huang, H. (2016). robust semi-parametric test detecting trait-dependent diversification. Systematic biology, 65(2), 181-193. https://doi.org/10.1093/sysbio/syv066. function extension original BAMMtools::traitDependentBAMM() function used carry STRAPP test extant time-calibrated phylogenies. Tests can carried speciation, extinction net diversification rates. deepSTRAPP::compute_STRAPP_test_for_focal_time() can handle three types statistical tests depending type trait data provided:

title: Computes STRAPP to test for a relationship between diversification rates and trait data — compute_STRAPP_test_for_focal_time
text: set functions carries STructured RAte Permutations Phylogenies (STRAPP) test defined Rabosky, D. L., & Huang, H. (2016). robust semi-parametric test detecting trait-dependent diversification. Systematic biology, 65(2), 181-193. extension original BAMMtools::traitDependentBAMM() function used carry STRAPP test extant time-calibrated phylogenies, allowing test differences/correlations point past (.e. focal_time). takes object class "bammdata" (BAMM_object) updated diversification rates ($tipLambda $tipMu) regimes ($tipStates) reflecting values observed specific time past (.e. $focal_time). Similarly, takes list (trait_data_list) provides $trait_data observed branches focal_time diversification rates regimes. STRAPP test carried drawing random set posterior samples BAMM_object, randomly permuting rates across blocks tips defined macroevolutionary regimes. Test statistics computed across initial observed data permuted data sample. two-tailed test, p-value proportion posterior samples test stats extreme permuted observed data. one-tailed test, p-value proportion posterior samples test stats higher permuted observed data. ———-  Major changes compared BAMMtools::traitDependentBAMM()  ———- Allow choose random sampling posterior configurations must done replacement replace_samples. Add post hoc pairwise tests (Dunn test) multinominal data. Use posthoc_pairwise_tests = TRUE. Provide outputs tailored histogram plots plot_histogram_STRAPP_test_for_focal_time() p-value time-series plots plot_STRAPP_pvalues_over_time(). Add prints detailing test carried , null alternative hypotheses, significant level used rejected null hypothesis. (Enabled print_hypothesis = TRUE). Split function multiple sub-functions according type data ($trait_data_type). Prevent using Pearson's correlation tests applying log-transformation continuous data. rationale reason assume tip rates distributed normally log-normally. Thus, Spearman's rank correlation test favored.

code: # ----- Prepare data ----- #  # Load mammals phylogeny and data from the R package motmot (data included in deepSTRAPP) # Initial data source: Slater, 2013; DOI: 10.1111/2041-210X.12084  data(mammals, package = "deepSTRAPP")  mammals_tree <- mammals$mammal.phy mammals_data <- setNames(object = mammals$mammal.mass$mean,                          nm = row.names(mammals$mammal.mass))[mammals_tree$tip.label]  # Run a stochastic mapping based on a Brownian Motion model # for Ancestral Trait Estimates to obtain a "contMap" object mammals_contMap <- phytools::contMap(mammals_tree, x = mammals_data,                                      res = 100, # Number of time steps                                      plot = FALSE)  # Set focal time focal_time <- 80  # ----- Example 1: keep_tip_labels = TRUE ----- #  # Cut contMap to 80 Mya while keeping tip.label # on terminal branches with a unique descending tip. updated_contMap <- cut_contMap_for_focal_time(contMap = mammals_contMap,                                               focal_time = focal_time,                                               keep_tip_labels = TRUE)  # Plot node labels on initial stochastic map with cut-off plot_contMap(mammals_contMap, lwd = 2) ape::nodelabels() abline(v = max(phytools::nodeHeights(mammals_contMap$tree)[,2]) - title: Cuts the phylogeny for a given time in the past — cut_phylo_for_focal_time
code: # Load eel phylogeny from the R package phytools # Source: Collar et al., 2014; DOI: 10.1038/ncomms6505 library(phytools) #> Loading required package: ape #> Loading required package: maps data(eel.tree)  # ----- Example 1: keep_tip_labels = TRUE ----- #  # Cut tree to 30 Mya while keeping tip.label on terminal branches with a unique descending tip. cut_eel.tree <- cut_phylo_for_focal_time(tree = eel.tree, focal_time = 30, keep_tip_labels = TRUE)  # Plot internal node labels on initial tree with cut-off plot(eel.tree) abline(v = max(phytools::nodeHeights(eel.tree)[,2]) - 30, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2) nb_tips <- length(eel.tree$tip.label) nodelabels_in_cut_tree <- (nb_tips + 1):(nb_tips + eel.tree$Nnode) nodelabels_in_cut_tree[!(nodelabels_in_cut_tree %in% cut_eel.tree$initial_nodes_ID)] <- NA ape::nodelabels(text = nodelabels_in_cut_tree)   # Plot initial internal node labels on cut tree plot(cut_eel.tree) ape::nodelabels(text = cut_eel.tree$initial_nodes_ID)   # Plot edge labels on initial tree with cut-off plot(eel.tree) abline(v = max(phytools::nodeHeights(eel.tree)[,2]) - 30, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2) edgelabels_in_cut_tree <- 1:nrow(eel.tree$edge) edgelabels_in_cut_tree[!(1:nrow(eel.tree$edge) %in% cut_eel.tree$initial_edges_ID)] <- NA ape::edgelabels(text = edgelabels_in_cut_tree)   # Plot initial edge labels on cut tree plot(cut_eel.tree) ape::edgelabels(text = cut_eel.tree$initial_edges_ID)   # ----- Example 2: keep_tip_labels = FALSE ----- #  # Cut tree to 30 Mya without keeping tip.label on terminal branches with a unique descending tip. # All tip.labels are converted to their descending/tipward node ID cut_eel.tree <- cut_phylo_for_focal_time(tree = eel.tree, focal_time = 30, keep_tip_labels = FALSE) plot(cut_eel.tree)

code: extract_most_likely_states_from_densityMaps_for_focal_time(   densityMaps,   ace = NULL,   tip_data = NULL,   focal_time,   update_densityMaps = FALSE,   keep_tip_labels = TRUE )

title: Extracts categorical trait data mapped on a phylogeny at a given time in the past — extract_most_likely_states_from_densityMaps_for_focal_time
text: densityMaps List objects class "densityMap", typically generated prepare_trait_data(), contains phylogenetic tree associated posterior probability given state along branches. object (.e., densityMap) corresponds state. phylogenetic tree must rooted fully resolved/dichotomous, need ultrametric (can includes fossils). ace (Optional) Numerical matrix record posterior probabilities ancestral states internal nodes, obtained prepare_trait_data() output $ace slot. Rows internal nodes_ID. Columns states. Values posterior probabilities state per node. Needed provide accurate estimates ancestral states. tip_data (Optional) Named character string vector tip states. Names nodes_ID internal nodes. Needed provide accurate tip values. focal_time Integer. time, terms time distance present, tree mapping must cut. must smaller root age phylogeny. update_densityMaps Logical. Specify whether mapped phylogeny (densityMaps) provided input updated visualization returned among outputs. Default FALSE. update consists cutting branches mapping younger focal_time. keep_tip_labels Logical. Specify whether terminal branches single descendant tip must retained initial tip.label updated densityMaps. Default TRUE. Used update_map = TRUE.

title: Extracts categorical trait data mapped on a phylogeny at a given time in the past — extract_most_likely_states_from_densityMaps_for_focal_time
text: default, function returns list three elements. $trait_data named character string vector ML states found along branches overlapping focal_time. Names tip.label/tipward node ID. $focal_time Integer. time, terms time distance present, trait data extracted. $trait_data_type Character string. Define type trait data "categorical". Used downstream analyses select appropriate statistical processing. update_densityMaps = TRUE, output list four elements: $trait_data, $focal_time, $trait_data_type, $densityMaps. $densityMaps list objects class "densityMap" contains updated densityMap state, branches mapping younger focal_time cut . function also adds multiple useful sub-elements $densityMaps$tree elements. $root_age Integer. Stores age root tree. $nodes_ID_df Data.frame two columns. Provides conversion new_node_ID initial_node_ID. row node. $initial_nodes_ID Vector character strings. Provides initial ID internal nodes. Used plot internal node IDs labels ape::nodelabels(). $edges_ID_df Data.frame two columns. Provides conversion new_edge_ID initial_edge_ID. row edge/branch. $initial_edges_ID Vector character strings. Provides initial ID edges/branches. Used plot edge/branch IDs labels ape::edgelabels().

title: Extracts categorical trait data mapped on a phylogeny at a given time in the past — extract_most_likely_states_from_densityMaps_for_focal_time
text: mapped phylogeny (densityMaps) cut specific time past (.e. focal_time) current trait values overlapping edges/branches extracted. —– Extract trait_data —– likely states extracted posterior probabilities displayed densityMaps. state highest probability assigned tip cut branches focal_time. True ML estimates used tip_data /ace provided optional inputs. practice discrepancy negligible. —– Update densityMaps —– obtain updated densityMaps alongside trait data, set update_densityMaps = TRUE. update consists cutting branches mapping younger focal_time. branch single descendant tip cut keep_tip_labels = TRUE, leaf left labeled tip.label unique descendant tip. branch single descendant tip cut keep_tip_labels = FALSE, leaf left labeled node ID unique descendant tip. cases, branch multiple descendant tips (.e., clade) cut, leaf left labeled node ID MRCA cut-clade. categorical trait mapping densityMap ($tree$maps $tree$mapped.edge) updated accordingly removing mapping associated cut branches.

Using values interpolated in the contMap instead. # Extract from tip data and ML estimates of ancestral characters (values are true ML estimates) eel_test <- extract_most_likely_trait_values_from_contMap_for_focal_time(    contMap = eel_contMap,    ace = eel_ACE, tip_data = eel_data,    focal_time = focal_time,    update_contMap = TRUE) #> Warning: Values in 'tip_data' are not ordered as tip labels in the contMap$tree. #> They were reordered to follow tip labels.  ## Visualize outputs  # Print trait data eel_test$trait_data #>    Moringua_edwardsi Kaupichthys_nuchalis                   69  #>             52.70485             65.25449             71.66003  #>                   70                   81                   89  #>             79.15280             76.11928             86.04101  #>                  101                  103    Serrivomer_sector  #>             82.04332            100.55349             94.72769  #>  Paraconger_notialis    Moringua_javanica                  121  #>             75.04175             95.62468            108.30889  #>        Albula_vulpes  #>            105.09029   # Plot node labels on initial stochastic map with cut-off plot(eel_contMap) ape::nodelabels() abline(v = max(phytools::nodeHeights(eel_contMap$tree)[,2]) - focal_time,        col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)   # Plot updated contMap with initial node labels plot(eel_test$contMap) ape::nodelabels(text = eel_test$contMap$tree$initial_nodes_ID)   # ----- Example 2: Include fossils (Non-ultrametric tree) ----- #  ## Test with non-ultrametric trees like mammals in motmot  ## Prepare data  # Load mammals phylogeny and data from the R package motmot included within deepSTRAPP # Data source: Slater, 2013; DOI: 10.1111/2041-210X.12084 data("mammals", package = "deepSTRAPP")  mammals_tree <- mammals$mammal.phy mammals_data <- setNames(object = mammals$mammal.mass$mean,                          nm = row.names(mammals$mammal.mass))[mammals_tree$tip.label]  # Get Ancestral Character Estimates based on a Brownian Motion model # To obtain values at internal nodes mammals_ACE <- phytools::fastAnc(tree = mammals_tree, x = mammals_data)  # Run a Stochastic Mapping based on a Brownian Motion model # to interpolate values along branches and obtain a "contMap" object mammals_contMap <- phytools::contMap(mammals_tree, x = mammals_data,                                      res = 100, # Number of time steps                                      plot = FALSE)  # Set focal time to 80 Mya focal_time <- 80  ## Extract trait data and update contMap for the given focal_time  # Extract from the contMap (values are not exact ML estimates) mammals_test <- extract_most_likely_trait_values_from_contMap_for_focal_time(    contMap = mammals_contMap,    focal_time = focal_time,    update_contMap = TRUE) #> WARNING: No ancestral character estimates (ace) for internal nodes have been provided. Using values interpolated in the contMap instead. #> WARNING: No tip data have been provided. Using values interpolated in the contMap instead. # Extract from tip data and ML estimates of ancestral characters (values are true ML) mammals_test <- extract_most_likely_trait_values_from_contMap_for_focal_time(    contMap = mammals_contMap,    ace = mammals_ACE, tip_data = mammals_data,    focal_time = focal_time,    update_contMap = TRUE)  ## Visualize outputs  # Print trait data mammals_test$trait_data #>            228            259            260            261            275  #>       6.137951       6.168691       6.097873       6.486549       7.170284  #>            336            340            348 Zalambdalestes     Asioryctes  #>       6.698360       7.821992       7.708320       3.930633       3.207854  #>   Ukhaatherium    Kennalestes            369     Mayulestes            390  #>       3.393016       2.681356       4.747897       4.935456       4.582359  #>     Turgidodon    Didelphodon       Pediomys Albertatherium    Asiatherium  #>       5.091326       6.097774       3.914626       4.448219       3.558069  #> Deltatheridium            410  #>       5.057019       6.170591   # Plot node labels on initial stochastic map with cut-off phytools::plot.contMap(mammals_contMap) ape::nodelabels() abline(v = max(phytools::nodeHeights(mammals_contMap$tree)[,2]) - focal_time,        col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)   # Plot updated contMap with initial node labels phytools::plot.contMap(mammals_test$contMap) ape::nodelabels(text = mammals_test$contMap$tree$initial_nodes_ID)

text: Plot time-calibrated phylogeny evolution diversification rates location regime shifts estimated BAMM (Bayesian Analysis Macroevolutionary Mixtures). branch colored accroding estimated rates speciation, extinction, net diversification stored object class bammdata. Rates can vary along time, thus colors evolved along individual branches. function wrapper original functions R package BAMMtools: Step 1: Use BAMMtools::plot.bammdata() map rates phylogeny. Step 2: Add location regime shifts BAMMtools::addBAMMshifts() (add_regime_shifts = TRUE).

title: Plot diversification rates and regime shifts from BAMM on phylogeny — plot_BAMM_rates
text: BAMM_object Object class "bammdata", typically generated prepare_diversification_data(), contains phylogenetic tree associated diversification rate mapping across selected posterior samples. works also BAMM_object updated specific focal_time using update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time(), deepSTRAPP workflow run_deepSTRAPP_for_focal_time run_deepSTRAPP_over_time(). rate_type character string specifying type diversification rates plot. Must one 'speciation', 'extinction' 'net_diversification' (default). method character string indicating method plotting phylogenetic tree. method = "phylogram" (default) plots phylogenetic tree using rectangular coordinates. method = "polar" plots phylogenetic tree using polar coordinates. add_regime_shifts Logical. Whether add location regime shifts phylogeny (Step 2). Default TRUE. configuration_type character string specifying select location regime shifts across posterior samples. configuration_type = "MAP": Use average locations recorded posterior samples Maximum Posteriori probability (MAP) configuration. regime shift configuration frequent configuration among posterior samples (See BAMMtools::getBestShiftConfiguration()). default option. configuration_type = "MSC": Use average locations recorded posterior samples Maximum Shift Credibility (MSC) configuration. regime shift configuration highest product marginal probabilities across branches (See BAMMtools::maximumShiftCredibility()). configuration_type = "index": Use configuration unique posterior sample index provided sample_index. sample_index Integer. Index posterior samples use plot location regime shifts. Used configuration_type = index. Default = 1. adjust_size_to_prob Logical. Whether scale size symbols showing location regime shifts according marginal shift probability shift happening location/branch. works $MSP_tree element summarizing marginal shift probabilities across branches BAMM_object. Default TRUE. regimes_fill Character string. Set color background symbols showing location regime shifts. Equivalent bg argument BAMMtools::addBAMMshifts(). Default "grey". regimes_size Numerical. Set size symbols showing location regime shifts. Equivalent cex argument BAMMtools::addBAMMshifts(). Default 1. regimes_pch Integer. Set shape symbols showing location regime shifts. Equivalent pch argument BAMMtools::addBAMMshifts(). Default 21. regimes_border_col Character string. Set color border symbols showing location regime shifts. Equivalent col argument BAMMtools::addBAMMshifts(). Default "black". regimes_border_width Numerical. Set width border symbols showing location regime shifts. Equivalent lwd argument BAMMtools::addBAMMshifts(). Default 1. ... Additional graphical arguments pass BAMMtools::plot.bammdata(), BAMMtools::addBAMMshifts(), par(). display_plot Logical. Whether display plot generated R console. Default TRUE. PDF_file_path Character string. provided, plot saved PDF file following path provided . path must end '.pdf'.

title: Plot diversification rates and regime shifts from BAMM on phylogeny — plot_BAMM_rates
text: function returns (invisibly) list three three elements similarly BAMMtools::plot.bammdata(). $coords: matrix plot coordinates. Rows correspond branches. Columns 1-2 starting (x,y) coordinates branch columns 3-4 ending (x,y) coordinates branch. method = "polar" fifth column gives angle(radians) branch. $colorbreaks: vector percentiles used group macroevolutionary rates color bins. $colordens: matrix kernel density estimates (column 2) evolutionary rates (column 1) color (column 3) corresponding rate value.

text: main input BAMM_object typical output prepare_diversification_data(). provides information rates regimes shifts across posterior samples BAMM. $MAP_BAMM_object $MSC_BAMM_object elements required plot regime shift locations following "MAP" "MSC" configuration_type respectively. $MSP_tree element required scale size symbols showing location regime shifts according marginal shift probabilities. (adjust_size_to_prob = TRUE). default option display regime shift use average locations posterior samples Maximum Posteriori probability (MAP) configuration. However, sometimes, multiple configurations similarly high frequency posterior samples (See BAMMtools::credibleShiftSet(). alternative use average locations posterior samples Maximum Shift Credibility (MSC) configuration instead. regime shift configuration highest product marginal probabilities across branches shift estimated. may differ MAP configuration. (See BAMMtools::maximumShiftCredibility()).

code: # Load BAMM output data(whale_BAMM_object, package = "deepSTRAPP")  ## Plot overall mean rates with MAP configuration for regime shifts # (rates are averaged only all posterior samples) plot_BAMM_rates(whale_BAMM_object, add_regime_shifts = TRUE,                 configuration_type = "MAP", bg = "black",                 regimes_size = 3)  ## Plot overall mean rates with MSC configuration for regime shifts # (rates are averaged only all posterior samples) plot_BAMM_rates(whale_BAMM_object, add_regime_shifts = TRUE,                 configuration_type = "MSC", bg = "black",                 regimes_size = 3)   ## Plot mean MAP rates with regime shifts # (rates are averaged only across MAP samples) plot_BAMM_rates(whale_BAMM_object$MAP_BAMM_object, add_regime_shifts = TRUE,                 configuration_type = "index",                 # Set to index to use the regime shift data from the '$MAP_BAMM_object'                 regimes_size = 3, bg = "black")  ## Plot mean MSC rates (rates averaged only across MSC samples) with regime shifts # (rates averaged only across MSC samples) plot_BAMM_rates(whale_BAMM_object$MSC_BAMM_object, add_regime_shifts = TRUE,                 configuration_type = "index",                 # Set to index to use the regime shift data from the '$MSC_BAMM_object'                 regimes_size = 3, bg = "black")

Whether display histograms generated R console. Default TRUE. plot_posthoc_tests Logical. multinominal data . title: Plot evolution of diversification rates in relation to trait values over time — plot_rates_through_time
text: deepSTRAPP_outputs List elements generated run_deepSTRAPP_over_time(), summarize results multiple STRAPP tests across $time_steps. list needs include two data.frame: $trait_data_df_over_time $diversification_data_df_over_time setting extract_trait_data_melted_df = TRUE extract_diversification_data_melted_df = TRUE. rate_type character string specifying type diversification rates use. Must one 'speciation', 'extinction' 'net_diversification' (default). Even deepSTRAPP_outputs object generated run_deepSTRAPP_over_time() testing another type rates, $trait_data_df_over_time $diversification_data_df_over_time data frames contain data types rates. quantile_ranges Vector numerical. continuous trait data. Quantiles used thresholds group branches trait values. must start 0 finish 1. Default c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) produces four balanced quantile groups. select_trait_levels (Vector ) character string. categorical biogeographic trait data. provide list subset states/ranges plot. Names must match ones found deepSTRAPP_outputs$trait_data_df_over_time$trait_value. Default means states/ranges plotted. time_range Vector two numerical values. Time boundaries used plot. NULL (default), range data provided deepSTRAPP_outputs used. color_scale Vector character string. List colors use build color scale grDevices::colorRampPalette() display quantile groups used discretize continuous trait data. lowest values highest values. continuous data. Default = NULL use 'Spectral' color palette RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(). colors_per_levels Named character string. set colors use plot rates state/range. Names = states/ranges; values = colors. NULL (default), default ggplot2 color palette (scales::hue_pal()) used. categorical biogeographic data. plot_CI Logical. Whether plot confidence interval (CI) based distribution rates found posterior samples. Default FALSE. CI_type Character string. select type confidence interval (CI) plot. fuzzy (default): overlay evolution rates found posterior samples high transparency levels. quantiles_rect: add polygon encompassing proportion rate values found posterior samples. proportion defined CI_quantiles. CI_quantiles Numerical. Proportion rate values across posterior samples encompassed confidence interval. CI_type = "quantiles_rect". Default 0.95. display_plot Logical. Whether display plot generated R console. Default TRUE. PDF_file_path Character string. provided, plot saved PDF file following path provided . path must end '.pdf'. return_mean_data_per_samples_df Logical. Whether include output data.frame mean rates per trait values computed posterior sample time-step (aggregated across groups branches based trait data). used draw confidence interval. Default FALSE. return_median_data_across_samples_df Logical. Whether include output data.frame median rates per trait values across posterior samples computed time-step (aggregated across groups branches based trait data posterior samples). used draw lines plot. Default FALSE.

Optional summary data frames: mean_data_per_samples_df data.frame four columns providing $mean_rates observed along branches similar $trait_value (categorical biogeographic) falling $quantile_ranges. Data extracted posterior sample ($BAMM_sample_ID) time-step (.e., $focal_time). used draw confidence interval. Included return_mean_data_per_samples_df = TRUE. $median_data_across_samples_df data.frame three columns providing $median_rates observed across posterior samples $mean_data_per_samples_df. used draw lines plot. Included return_median_data_across_samples_df = TRUE. PDF_file_path provided, function also generate PDF file plot.

title: Run a full BAMM (Bayesian Analysis of Macroevolutionary Mixtures) workflow — prepare_diversification_data
text: Run full BAMM (Bayesian Analysis Macroevolutionary Mixtures) workflow produce BAMM_object contains phylogenetic tree associated diversification rates mapped along branches, across selected posterior samples: Step 1: Set BAMM - Record BAMM settings generate input files needed BAMM. Step 2: Run BAMM - Run BAMM move output files dedicated directory. Step 3: Evaluate BAMM - Produce evaluation plots ESS data. Step 4: Import BAMM outputs - Load BAMM_object R subset posterior samples. Step 5: Clean BAMM files - Remove files generated BAMM run. BAMM_object output typically used input run deepSTRAPP run_deepSTRAPP_for_focal_time() run_deepSTRAPP_over_time(). Diversification rates regimes shift can visualized plot_BAMM_rates(). BAMM model diversification time-calibrated phylogenies explores complex diversification dynamics allowing multiple regime shifts across clades without priori hypotheses location shifts. uses reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (rjMCMC) automatically explore vast range models different speciation extinction rates, different number location regime shits. function work BAMM C++ program installed machine. See BAMM website: http://bamm-project.org/ companion R package BAMMtools.

title: Run a full BAMM (Bayesian Analysis of Macroevolutionary Mixtures) workflow — prepare_diversification_data
text: BAMM_install_directory_path Character string. path directory BAMM . Use '/' separate directory sub-directories. path must end '/'. phylo Time-calibrated phylogeny. Object class "phylo" defined R package ape. phylogeny must rooted fully resolved. BAMM currently work fossils, tree must also ultrametric. prefix_for_files Character string. Prefix add BAMM files stored BAMM_output_directory_path keep_BAMM_outputs = TRUE. Files exported 'prefix_*' underscore separating prefix file name. Default NULL (prefix added). seed Integer. Set seed ensure reproducibility. Default NULL (random seed used). numberOfGenerations Integer. Number steps MCMC run. set high enough reach equilibrium distribution allows posterior samples uncorrelated. Check Effective Sample Size parameters coda::effectiveSize() Evaluation step. Default value 10^7. globalSamplingFraction Numerical. Global sampling fraction representing overall proportion terminals phylogeny compared estimated overall richness clade. acts multiplier rates needed achieve extant diversity. Default 1.0 (assuming taxa phylogeny). sampleProbsFilename Character string. path .txt file used provide clade-specific sampling fractions. See BAMMtools::samplingProbs() generate file. provided, globalSamplingFraction ignored. expectedNumberOfShifts Integer. Set expected number regime shifts. acts hyperparameter controlling exponential prior distribution used modulate reversible jumps across model configurations rjMCMC run. set NULL (default), empirical rule used define value: 1 regime shift expected every 100 tips phylogeny, minimum 1. best practice consists trying several values inspect similarity prior posterior distribution regime shift parameter. See BAMMtools::plotPrior() Evaluation step produce evaluation plot. eventDataWriteFreq Integer. Set frequency write event data output file = sampling frequency posterior samples. set NULL (default), set frequency 2000 posterior samples recorded eventDataWriteFreq = numberOfGenerations / 2000. burn_in Numerical. Proportion posterior samples removed BAMM output ensure remaining samples drawn equilibrium distribution reached. can evaluated looking MCMC trace (see Evaluation step). Default 0.25. nb_posterior_samples Numerical. Number posterior samples extract, removing burn-, final BAMM_object use downstream analyses. Default = 1000. additional_BAMM_settings List named elements. Additional settings options BAMM provided list named arguments. Ex: list(lambdaInit0 = 0.5, muInit0 = 0). See available settings template file provided within deepSTRAPP package files 'BAMM_template_diversification.txt'. template can also loaded directly R utils::data(BAMM_template_diversification) displayed print(BAMM_template_diversification). BAMM_output_directory_path Character string. path directory used store input/output files generated. Use '/' separate directory subdirectories. must end '/'. Default ./BAMM_outputs/ keep_BAMM_outputs Logical. Whether BAMM_output_directory kept run. Default = TRUE. MAP_odd_ratio_threshold Numerical. Controls definition 'core-shifts' used distinguish across configurations fetching MAP samples. Shifts odd-ratio marginal posterior probability / prior lower MAP_odd_ratio_threshold ignored. See BAMMtools::getBestShiftConfiguration(). Default = 5. skip_evaluations Logical. Whether skip Evaluation step including MCMC trace, ESS, prior/posterior comparisons expected number shifts. Default = FALSE. plot_evaluations Logical. Whether display plots generated Evaluation step: MCMC trace, prior/posterior comparisons expected number shifts. Default = TRUE. save_evaluations Logical. Whether save outputs evaluations table (ESS), PDFs (MCMC trace, prior/posterior comparisons expected number shifts) BAMM_output_directory. Default = TRUE.

title: Run a full BAMM (Bayesian Analysis of Macroevolutionary Mixtures) workflow — prepare_diversification_data
text: function runs full BAMM (Bayesian Analysis Macroevolutionary Mixtures) workflow produce BAMM_object contains phylogenetic tree associated diversification rates mapped along branches, across selected posterior samples. Step 1: Set BAMM Produces tree file phylogeny. Default file: 'phylogeny.tree'. Save configuration settings used BAMM run. Default file: 'config_file.txt'. Save default priors generated BAMMtools::setBAMMpriors based phylogeny. Default file: 'priors.txt'. Step 2: Run BAMM Run BAMM using system console Move output files dedicated BAMM_output_directory. Default directory ./BAMM_outputs/. 'run_info.txt' containing summary parameters/settings. 'mcmc_log.txt' containing raw MCMC information useful diagnosing convergence. 'event_data.txt' containing evolutionary rate parameters topological mappings. 'chain_swap.txt' containing data chain swap proposal (proposal occurred, chains might swapped, whether swap accepted). 'acceptance_info.txt' containing history acceptance/proposal MCMC steps (additional setting outputAcceptanceInfo set 1). Step 3: Evaluate BAMM Plot MCMC trace = evolution logLik across MCMC generations. Output file = 'MCMC_trace_logLik.pdf'. Compute Effective Sample Size (ESS) across posterior samples (removing burn-) using coda::effectiveSize(). way evaluate MCMC runs enough generations produce robust estimates. Ideally, ESS higher 200. Output file = 'ESS_df.csv'. Plot comparison prior posterior distributions number regime shifts BAMMtools::plotPrior. Output file = 'PP_nb_shifts_plot.pdf'. good value expectedNumberOfShifts one high similarities distributions hinting information data coincides expectations number regime shifts. best practice consists trying several values control affects final output. Step 4: Import BAMM outputs Load BAMM outputs BAMMtools::getEventData. Subset posterior samples requested nb_posterior_samples BAMMtools::subsetEventData. Record $expectedNumberOfShifts used set prior. useful downstream analyses involving comparison prior vs. posterior probabilities (See BAMMtools::distinctShiftConfigurations()). Record marginal posterior probability regime shift along branches based proportion samples harboring regime shift along branch. (See BAMMtools::marginalShiftProbsTree()). Result stored $MSP_tree phylogenetic tree $edge.length scaled marginal posterior probability. Extract Maximum Posteriori probability (MAP) configuration = configuration regime shift location found frequently among posterior samples. (See BAMMtools::getBestShiftConfiguration()). ignores shifts odd-ratio marginal posterior probability / prior lower MAP_odd_ratio_threshold avoid noise non-core shifts. MAP sample indices stored $MAP_indices. Diversification rates shift locations branches averaged across MAP samples recorded object class "bammdata" $MAP_BAMM_object single $eventData table used plot regime shifts phylogeny plot_BAMM_rates(). Extract Maximum Shift Credibility (MSC) configuration = configuration regime shift location highest product marginal probabilities across branches. (See BAMMtools::maximumShiftCredibility()). MSC sample indices stored $MSC_indices. Diversification rates shift locations branches averaged across MSC samples recorded object class "bammdata" $MSC_BAMM_object single $eventData table used plot regime shifts phylogeny plot_BAMM_rates(). Step 5: Clean BAMM files Remove files generated Steps 1 & 2 keep_BAMM_outputs = FALSE. Delete BAMM_output_directory empty cleaning files. BAMM_object output: typically used input run deepSTRAPP run_deepSTRAPP_for_focal_time() run_deepSTRAPP_over_time(). can used extract rates regimes focal_time past update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time(). can used map diversification rates regime shifts phylogeny plot_BAMM_rates().

Step 3: Infer ancestral characters estimates (ACE) nodes. Step 4: Run stochastic mapping simulations generate evolutionary histories compatible best model inferred ACE. (categorical biogeographic data) Step 5: Infer ancestral states along branches. continuous traits: use interpolation produce contMap. categorical biogeographic data: compute posterior frequencies state/range produce densityMap state/range.

title: Map trait evolution on a time-calibrated phylogeny — prepare_trait_data
text: Map trait evolution time-calibrated phylogeny several steps: Step 1: Models fit using Maximum Likelihood approach: "continuous" data models fit geiger::fitContinuous(): "BM", "OU", "EB", "rate_trend", "lambda", "kappa", "delta". Default "BM". "categorical" data models fit geiger::fitDiscrete(): "ER", "SYM", "ARD", "meristic", "matrix". Default "ARD". "biogeographic" data models fit R package BioGeoBEARS: "BAYAREALIKE", "DIVALIKE", "DEC", "BAYAREALIKE+J", "DIVALIKE+J", "DEC+J". Default "DEC". Step 2: Best model identified among list evolutionary_models comparing corrected AIC (AICc) selecting  model lowest AICc. Step 3: continuous traits: Ancestral characters estimates (ACE) inferred phytools::fastAnc tree modified branch lengths scaled reflect evolutionary rates estimated best model using phytools::rescale(). Step 4: Stochastic Mapping. categorical biogeographic data, stochastic mapping simulations performed generate evolutionary histories compatible best model inferred ACE. Node states/ranges drawn scaled marginal likelihoods ACE, states/ranges shifts along branches simulated according transition matrix Q estimated best fitting model. Step 5: Infer ancestral states along branches. continuous traits: ancestral trait values along branches interpolated phytools::contMap(). provides quick estimates trait value point time, provide accurate ML estimates case models time trait-value dependent ("EB" "OU") interpolation used built contMap assuming constant rate along branch. However, ancestral trait values nodes remain accurate categorical biogeographic data: compute posterior frequencies state/range among simulated evolutionary histories (simmaps) produce densityMap state/range reflects changes along branches probability harboring given state/range.

title: Runs deepSTRAPP to test for a relationship between diversification rates and trait data at a given focal time — run_deepSTRAPP_for_focal_time
text: compute_STRAPP_test_for_focal_time() carries appropriate statistical method test relationship diversification rates trait data given point past (.e. focal_time). can handle three types statistical tests depending type trait data provided: Continuous trait data: Test correlations Spearman's rank correlation test (See stats::cor.test). Binary trait data (two states): Test differences rates states Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon rank-sum test (See stats::wilcox.test). Multinominal trait data (two states): Test differences rates across states Kruskal-Wallis H test (See stats::kruskal.test). posthoc_pairwise_tests = TRUE, Dunn's post hoc pairwise rank-sum tests pairs states carried (See dunn.test::dunn.test).

text: Wrapper function run deepSTRAPP workflows multiple time steps past. starts traits mapped phylogeny (trait data) BAMM output (diversification data) carries appropriate statistical method test relationship diversification rates trait data. workflow repeated multiple points time (.e. time_steps) results summarized data.frame. function can also provide summaries trait values diversification rates extracted along branches different time_steps. Statistical tests based block-permutations: rates data randomized across tips following blocks defined diversification regimes identified tip (typically BAMM). tests called STructured RAte Permutations Phylogenies (STRAPP) described Rabosky, D. L., & Huang, H. (2016). robust semi-parametric test detecting trait-dependent diversification. Systematic biology, 65(2), 181-193. https://doi.org/10.1093/sysbio/syv066. See original BAMMtools::traitDependentBAMM() function used carry STRAPP test extant time-calibrated phylogenies. Tests can carried speciation, extinction net diversification rates.

code: # Load phylogeny and tip data library(phytools) data(eel.tree) data(eel.data)  # Transform feeding mode data into biogeographic data with ranges A, B, and AB. eel_data <- stats::setNames(eel.data$feed_mode, rownames(eel.data)) eel_data <- as.character(eel_data) eel_data[eel_data == "bite"] <- "A" eel_data[eel_data == "suction"] <- "B" eel_data[c(5, 6, 7, 15, 25, 32, 33, 34, 50, 52, 57, 58, 59)] <- "AB" eel_data <- stats::setNames(eel_data, rownames(eel.data)) table(eel_data) #> eel_data #>  A AB  B  #> 27 13 21   colors_per_levels <- c("dodgerblue3", "gold") names(colors_per_levels) <- c("A", "B")  ### Uncomment to run ###  # ## Prepare phylo # # # Set path to BioGeoBEARS directory # BioGeoBEARS_directory_path = "./BioGeoBEARS_directory/" # # # Export phylo # path_to_phylo <- BioGeoBEARS::np(paste0(BioGeoBEARS_directory_path, "phylo.tree")) # write.tree(phy = eel.tree, file = path_to_phylo) # # ## Prepare range data # # tip_data <- eel_data # # Convert tip_data to df # ranges_df <- as.data.frame(tip_data) # # Get list of all unique areas # unique_areas_in_ranges_list <- strsplit(x = tip_data, split = "") # unique_areas <- unique(unlist(unique_areas_in_ranges_list)) # unique_areas <- unique_areas[order(unique_areas)] # # # Loop per unique areas # for (i in seq_along(unique_areas)) # { #   # i <- 1 # #   # Extract unique area #   unique_area_i <- unique_areas[i] #   # Detect presence in ranges #   binary_match_i <- unlist(lapply(X = unique_areas_in_ranges_list, #      FUN = function (x) { unique_area_i %in% x } )) # #   # Add to ranges_df #   ranges_df <- cbind(ranges_df, binary_match_i) # } # # Extract binary df of presence/absence # binary_df <- ranges_df[, -1] # Convert character strings into numerical factors # binary_df_num <- as.data.frame(apply(X = binary_df, MARGIN = 2, FUN = as.numeric)) # row.names(binary_df_num) <- names(tip_data) # names(binary_df_num) <- unique_areas # # # Produce tipranges object from numeric df # Taxa_bioregions_tipranges_obj <- BioGeoBEARS::define_tipranges_object(tmpdf = binary_df_num) # # # Set path to tip ranges object # path_to_tip_ranges <- BioGeoBEARS::np(paste0(BioGeoBEARS_directory_path,"tip_ranges.data")) # # # Export tip ranges in Lagrange/PHYLIP format # BioGeoBEARS::save_tipranges_to_LagrangePHYLIP( #   tipranges_object = Taxa_bioregions_tipranges_obj, #   lgdata_fn = path_to_tip_ranges, #   areanames = colnames(Taxa_bioregions_tipranges_obj@df)) # # ## Prepare models # # # Prepare DEC model run # DEC_run <- BioGeoBEARS::define_BioGeoBEARS_run( #    num_cores_to_use = 1, #    max_range_size = 2, # To set the maximum number of bioregion encompassed #       # by a lineage range at any time #    trfn = path_to_phylo, # To provide path to the input tree file #    geogfn = path_to_tip_ranges, # To provide path to the LagrangePHYLIP file with binary ranges #    return_condlikes_table = TRUE, # To ask to obtain all marginal likelihoods #       # computed by the model and used to display ancestral states #    print_optim = TRUE) # # # Check that starting parameter values are inside the min/max # DEC_run <- BioGeoBEARS::fix_BioGeoBEARS_params_minmax(BioGeoBEARS_run_object = DEC_run) # # Check validity of set-up before run # BioGeoBEARS::check_BioGeoBEARS_run(DEC_run) # # # Use the DEC model as template for DEC+J model # DEC_J_run <- DEC_run # # # Update status of jump speciation parameter to be estimated # DEC_J_run$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","type"] <- "free" # # Set initial value of J for optimization to an arbitrary low non-null value # j_start <- 0.0001 # DEC_J_run$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","init"] <- j_start # DEC_J_run$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["j","est"] <- j_start # # # Check validity of set-up before run # DEC_J_run <- BioGeoBEARS::fix_BioGeoBEARS_params_minmax(BioGeoBEARS_run_object = DEC_J_run) # invisible(BioGeoBEARS::check_BioGeoBEARS_run(DEC_J_run)) # # ## Run models # # # Run DEC model # DEC_fit <- BioGeoBEARS::bears_optim_run(DEC_run) # # # Set starting values for optimization of DEC+J model based on MLE in the DEC model # d_start <- DEC_fit$outputs@params_table["d","est"] # e_start <- DEC_fit$outputs@params_table["e","est"] # # DEC_J_run$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","init"] <- d_start # DEC_J_run$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["d","est"] <- d_start # DEC_J_run$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["e","init"] <- e_start # DEC_J_run$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["e","est"] <- e_start # # # Run DEC+J model # DEC_J_fit <- BioGeoBEARS::bears_optim_run(DEC_J_run) # # ## Store model outputs # list_model_fits <- list(DEC = DEC_fit, DEC_J = DEC_J_fit) # # ## Compare models # model_comparison_output <- select_best_model_from_BioGeoBEARS(list_model_fits = list_model_fits) # # # Explore output # str(model_comparison_output, max.level = 1) # # Print comparison # print(model_comparison_output$models_comparison_df) # # Print best model fit # print(model_comparison_output$best_model_fit$outputs) #

code: # ----- Example 1: Continuous data ----- #  # Load phylogeny and tip data library(phytools) data(eel.tree) data(eel.data)  # Extract body size eel_data <- stats::setNames(eel.data$Max_TL_cm,                             rownames(eel.data))  # Fit BM model BM_fit <- geiger::fitContinuous(phy = eel.tree, dat = eel_data, model = "BM") # Fit EB model EB_fit <- geiger::fitContinuous(phy = eel.tree, dat = eel_data, model = "EB") #> Warning:  #> Parameter estimates appear at bounds: #> 	a # Fit OU model OU_fit <- geiger::fitContinuous(phy = eel.tree, dat = eel_data, model = "OU")  # Store models list_model_fits <- list(BM = BM_fit, EB = EB_fit, OU = OU_fit)  # Compare models model_comparison_output <- select_best_trait_model_from_geiger(list_model_fits = list_model_fits)  # Explore output str(model_comparison_output, max.level = 2) #> List of 3 #>  $ models_comparison_df:'data.frame':	3 obs. of  6 variables: #>   ..$ model         : chr [1:3] "BM" "EB" "OU" #>   ..$ logL          : num [1:3] -339 -339 -329 #>   ..$ k             : num [1:3] 2 3 3 #>   ..$ AICc          : num [1:3] 682 684 665 #>   ..$ Akaike_weights: 'aic.w' num [1:3] 0 0 100 #>   ..$ rank          : int [1:3] 2 3 1 #>  $ best_model_name     : chr "OU" #>  $ best_model_fit      :List of 4 #>   ..$ lik:function (pars, ...)   #>   .. ..- attr(*, "argn")= chr [1:2] "alpha" "sigsq" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "cache")=List of 26 #>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "bm" "function" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "model")= chr "OU" #>   ..$ bnd:'data.frame':	2 obs. of  2 variables: #>   ..$ res: num [1:100, 1:4] 4.77e-81 1.84e-76 4.34e-02 1.74e-217 4.11e-97 ... #>   .. ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2 #>   ..$ opt:List of 8 #>   ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "gfit" "list" # Print comparison print(model_comparison_output$models_comparison_df) #>    model      logL k     AICc Akaike_weights rank #> BM    BM -338.9352 2 682.0773              0    2 #> EB    EB -338.9355 3 684.2921              0    3 #> OU    OU -329.2538 3 664.9287            100    1 # Print best model fit print(model_comparison_output$best_model_fit) #> GEIGER-fitted comparative model of continuous data #>  fitted ‘OU’ model parameters: #> 	alpha = 0.043393 #> 	sigsq = 278.039659 #> 	z0 = 92.068484 #>  #>  model summary: #> 	log-likelihood = -329.253814 #> 	AIC = 664.507628 #> 	AICc = 664.928681 #> 	free parameters = 3 #>  #> Convergence diagnostics: #> 	optimization iterations = 100 #> 	failed iterations = 0 #> 	number of iterations with same best fit = 8 #> 	frequency of best fit = 0.080 #>  #>  object summary: #> 	'lik' -- likelihood function #> 	'bnd' -- bounds for likelihood search #> 	'res' -- optimization iteration summary #> 	'opt' -- maximum likelihood parameter estimates  # ----- Example 2: Categorical data ----- #  # Load phylogeny and tip data library(phytools) data(eel.tree) data(eel.data)  # Extract feeding mode data eel_data <- stats::setNames(eel.data$feed_mode, rownames(eel.data)) table(eel_data) #> eel_data #>    bite suction  #>      31      30   # Fit ER model ER_fit <- geiger::fitDiscrete(phy = eel.tree, dat = eel_data, model = "ER") # Fit ARD model ARD_fit <- geiger::fitDiscrete(phy = eel.tree, dat = eel_data, model = "ARD")  # Store models list_model_fits <- list(ER = ER_fit, ARD = ARD_fit)  # Compare models model_comparison_output <- select_best_trait_model_from_geiger(list_model_fits = list_model_fits)  # Explore output str(model_comparison_output, max.level = 2) #> List of 3 #>  $ models_comparison_df:'data.frame':	2 obs. of  6 variables: #>   ..$ model         : chr [1:2] "ER" "ARD" #>   ..$ logL          : num [1:2] -37 -37 #>   ..$ k             : int [1:2] 1 2 #>   ..$ AICc          : num [1:2] 76.1 78.2 #>   ..$ Akaike_weights: 'aic.w' num [1:2] 74.1 25.9 #>   ..$ rank          : int [1:2] 1 2 #>  $ best_model_name     : chr "ER" #>  $ best_model_fit      :List of 4 #>   ..$ lik:function (pars, ...)   #>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:4] "constrained" "mkn" "dtlik" "function" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "argn")= chr "q12" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "formulae")=List of 1 #>   .. ..- attr(*, "func")=function (pars, ...)   #>   .. .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:3] "mkn" "dtlik" "function" #>   .. .. ..- attr(*, "argn")= chr [1:2] "q12" "q21" #>   .. .. ..- attr(*, "levels")= chr [1:2] "bite" "suction" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "levels")= chr [1:2] "bite" "suction" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "trns")= logi TRUE #>   .. ..- attr(*, "transform")= chr "none" #>   ..$ bnd:'data.frame':	2 obs. of  2 variables: #>   ..$ res: num [1:100, 1:3] 0.0157 0.0157 0.0157 0.0157 0.0157 ... #>   .. ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2 #>   ..$ opt:List of 7 #>   ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "gfit" "list" # title: Updates diversification rates/regimes mapped on a phylogeny up to a given time in the past — update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time
text: Updates object class "bammdata" obtain diversification rates/regimes found along branches specific time past (.e. focal_time). Optionally, function can update object display mapped phylogeny branches overlapping focal_time shorten focal_time.

code: update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time(   BAMM_object,   focal_time,   update_rates = TRUE,   update_regimes = TRUE,   update_tree = FALSE,   update_plot = FALSE,   update_all_elements = FALSE,   keep_tip_labels = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Updates diversification rates/regimes mapped on a phylogeny up to a given time in the past — update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time
text: BAMM_object Object class "bammdata", typically generated prepare_diversification_data(), contains phylogenetic tree associated diversification rate mapping across selected posterior samples. phylogenetic tree must rooted fully resolved/dichotomous, need ultrametric (can includes fossils). focal_time Numerical. time, terms time distance present, tree rate mapping must cut. must smaller root age phylogeny. update_rates Logical. Specify whether diversification rates stored $tipLambda (speciation) $tipMu (extinction) must updated summarize rates found along branches focal_time. Default TRUE. update_regimes Logical. Specify whether diversification regimes stored $tipStates must updated summarize regimes found along branches focal_time. Default TRUE. update_tree Logical. Specify whether update phylogeny branches younger focal_time cut-. Default FALSE. update_plot Logical. Specify whether update phylogeny elements used plot_BAMM_rates() plot diversification rates phylogeny branches younger focal_time cut-. Default FALSE. set TRUE, override update_tree parameter update phylogeny. update_all_elements Logical. Specify whether update elements object, including rates/regimes/phylogeny/elements plot_BAMM_rates()/elements. Default FALSE. set TRUE, override update_* parameters update elements. keep_tip_labels Logical. terminal branches single descendant tip retain initial tip.label updated phylogeny diversification rate mapping? Default TRUE. set FALSE, tipward node ID used label tips. verbose Logical. progression displayed? message printed every batch 100 BAMM posterior samples updated. Default TRUE.

title: Updates diversification rates/regimes mapped on a phylogeny up to a given time in the past — update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time
text: function returns list updated BAMM_object class "bammdata". Phylogeny-related elements used plot phylogeny ape::plot.phylo(): $edge Matrix integers. Defines tree topology providing rootward tipward node ID edge. $Nnode Integer. Number internal nodes. $tip.label Vector character strings. Labels tips, including fossils older focal_time present. keep_tip_labels = TRUE, cut-branches single descendant tip retain initial tip.label. keep_tip_labels = FALSE, cut-branches labeled using tipward node ID. $edge.length Vector numerical. Length edges/branches. $node.label Vector character strings. Labels internal nodes. (Present present initial BAMM_object) BAMM internal elements used tree exploration: $begin Vector numerical. Absolute time since root edge/branch start (rootward). $end Vector numerical.  Absolute time since root edge/branch end (tipward). $downseq Vector integers. Order node visits using pre-order tree traversal. $lastvisit ID last node visited starting node corresponding position $downseq. BAMM elements summarizing diversification data: $numberEvents Vector integer. Number events/macroevolutionary regimes (k+1) recorded posterior configuration. k = number shifts. $eventData List data.frames. One per posterior sample. Records shift events macroevolutionary regimes parameters. 1st line = Background root regime. $eventVectors List integer vectors. One per posterior sample. Record regime ID per branches. $tipStates List named integer vectors. One per posterior sample. Record regime ID per tips present focal_time. Updated update_regimes = TRUE. $tipLambda List named numerical vectors. One per posterior sample. Record speciation rates per tips present focal_time. Updated update_rates = TRUE. $tipMu List named numerical vectors. One per posterior sample. Record extinction rates per tips present focal_time. Updated update_rates = TRUE. $eventBranchSegs List matrix numerical. One per posterior sample. Record regime ID per segments branches. $meanTipLambda Vector named numerical. Mean tip speciation rates across posterior configurations tips present focal_time (includes older fossils). $meanTipMu Vector named numerical. Mean tip extinction rates across posterior configurations tips present focal_time (includes older fossils). $type Character string. Set type data modeled BAMM. "diversification". Additional elements providing key information downstream analyses: $expectedNumberOfShifts Integer. expected number regime shifts used set prior BAMM. $MSP_tree Object class phylo. List 4 elements duplicating information Phylogeny-related elements , except $MSP_tree$edge.length recording Marginal Shift Probability branch (.e., probability regime shift occur along branch) whose origin older focal_time. $MAP_indices Vector integers. indices Maximum Posteriori probability (MAP) configurations among posterior samples. $MAP_BAMM_object. List 18 elements class "bammdata" recording mean rates regime shift locations found across Maximum Posteriori probability (MAP) configuration. BAMM elements summarizing diversification data holds single entry describing mean diversification history, updated focal_time`. $MSC_indices Vector integers. indices Maximum Shift Credibility (MSC) configurations among posterior samples. $MSC_BAMM_object List 18 elements class "bammdata" recording mean rates regime shift locations found across Maximum Shift Credibility (MSC) configurations. BAMM elements summarizing diversification data holds single entry describing mean diversification history, updated focal_time`. New elements added provide update information: $root_age Integer. Stores age root tree. $nodes_ID_df Data.frame two columns. Provides conversion new_node_ID initial_node_ID. row node. $initial_nodes_ID Vector character strings. Provides initial ID internal nodes. Used plot internal node IDs labels ape::nodelabels(). $edges_ID_df Data.frame two columns. Provides conversion new_edge_ID initial_edge_ID. row edge/branch. $initial_edges_ID Vector character strings. Provides initial ID edges/branches. Used plot edge/branch IDs labels ape::edgelabels(). $dtrates List three elements. 1/ $dtrates$tau Numerical. Resolution factor describing fraction segment length used plot_BAMM_rates() compared full depth initial tree (.e., root_age) 2/ $dtrates$rates List two numerical vectors. Speciation extinction rates along segments used plot_BAMM_rates(). 3/ $dtrates$tmat Matrix numerical. Start end times segments term distance root. $initial_colorbreaks List three vectors numerical. Rate values percentiles delimiting bins mapping rates colors BAMMtools::plot.bammdata(). element provides values different type rates ($speciation, $extinction, $net_diversification). $focal_time Integer. time, terms time distance present, rates/regimes extracted tree eventually cut.

title: Updates diversification rates/regimes mapped on a phylogeny up to a given time in the past — update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time
text: object class "bammdata" (BAMM_object) cut-specific time past (.e. focal_time) current diversification rate values overlapping edges/branches extracted. —– Update diversification rate data —– update_rates = TRUE, diversification rates branches overlapping focal_time updated. cut-branches form new tip present focal_time updated associated diversification rate data. Fossils older focal_time yield data. $tipLambda contains speciation rates. $tipMu contains extinction rates. update_regimes = TRUE, diversification regimes branches overlapping focal_time updated. cut-branches form new tip present focal_time updated associated diversification regime ID found $tipStates. Fossils older focal_time yield data. —– Update phylogeny —– update_tree = TRUE, elements defining phylogeny, "phylo" object updated branches younger focal_time cut-: $edge defines tree topology. $Nnode defines number internal nodes. $tip.label provides labels tips, including fossils older focal_time present. $edge.length provides length branches. $node.label provides labels internal nodes. (Optional) —– Update plot plot_BAMM_rates() —– update_plot = TRUE, elements used plot diversification rates phylogeny using plot_BAMM_rates() updated branches younger focal_time cut-: $begin provides absolute time since root edge/branch start (rootward). $end provides absolute time since root edge/branch end (tipward). $eventVectors provides regime membership per branches posterior sample configuration. $eventBranchSegs provides regime membership per segments branches posterior sample configuration. $dtrates provides mean speciation extinction rates along segments branches, resolution fraction (tau) describing fraction segment length compared full depth initial tree (.e., root_age).

Tip states/rates updated for BAMM posterior sample n°400/1000 #> 2025-09-18 18:18:53.539371 - Tip states/rates updated for BAMM posterior sample n°500/1000 #> 2025-09-18 18:18:53.733336 - Tip states/rates updated for BAMM posterior sample n°600/1000 #> 2025-09-18 18:18:53.914755 - Tip states/rates updated for BAMM posterior sample n°700/1000 #> 2025-09-18 18:18:54.124635 - Tip states/rates updated for BAMM posterior sample n°800/1000 #> 2025-09-18 18:18:54.308446 - Tip states/rates updated for BAMM posterior sample n°900/1000 #> 2025-09-18 18:18:54.495747 - Tip states/rates updated for BAMM posterior sample n°1000/1000  # Add "phylo" class to be compatible with phytools::nodeHeights() class(whale_BAMM_object) <- unique(c(class(whale_BAMM_object), "phylo")) root_age <- max(phytools::nodeHeights(whale_BAMM_object)[,2]) # Remove temporary "phylo" class class(whale_BAMM_object) <- setdiff(class(whale_BAMM_object), "phylo")  ## Plot initial BAMM_object for t = 0 My plot_BAMM_rates(whale_BAMM_object, add_regime_shifts = TRUE,                 labels = TRUE, legend = TRUE,                 par.reset = FALSE) # Keep plotting parameters in memory to use abline(). abline(v = root_age - focal_time,       col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)   ## Plot updated BAMM_object for t = 5 My plot_BAMM_rates(whale_BAMM_object_5My, add_regime_shifts = TRUE,                 labels = TRUE, legend = TRUE)   # ----- Example 2: Extant Ponerinae (1,534 taxa) ----- #  ## Load the BAMM_object summarizing 1000 posterior samples of BAMM data(Ponerinae_BAMM_object, package = "deepSTRAPP")  ## Set focal-time to 10 My focal_time = 10  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Update the BAMM object (May take several minutes to run) Ponerinae_BAMM_object_10My <- update_rates_and_regimes_for_focal_time(   BAMM_object = Ponerinae_BAMM_object,   focal_time = focal_time,   update_rates = TRUE, update_regimes = TRUE,   update_tree = TRUE, update_plot = TRUE,   update_all_elements = TRUE,   keep_tip_labels = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE) } # }  ## Load results to save time data(Ponerinae_BAMM_object_10My, package = "deepSTRAPP")  ## Extract root age # Add temporarily the "phylo" class to be compatible with phytools::nodeHeights() class(Ponerinae_BAMM_object) <- unique(c(class(Ponerinae_BAMM_object), "phylo")) root_age <- max(phytools::nodeHeights(Ponerinae_BAMM_object)[,2]) # Remove temporary "phylo" class class(Ponerinae_BAMM_object) <- setdiff(class(Ponerinae_BAMM_object), "phylo")  ## Plot diversification rates on the initial tree plot_BAMM_rates(Ponerinae_BAMM_object,                 legend = TRUE, labels = FALSE) abline(v = root_age - focal_time,        col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)   ## Plot diversification rates and regime shifts on the updated tree (cut-off for 10 My) # Keep the initial color scheme plot_BAMM_rates(Ponerinae_BAMM_object_10My, legend = TRUE, labels = FALSE,                 colorbreaks = Ponerinae_BAMM_object_10My$initial_colorbreaks$net_diversification)   # Use a new color scheme mapped on the new distribution of rates plot_BAMM_rates(Ponerinae_BAMM_object_10My, legend = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
